Hello Everyone,

Our team—Maria Joseph (@MARIA JOSEPH), Divakaran D (@Divakaran Divakaran), and I—have been working on a project formalizing Gaussian elimination. We would love some feedback on whether this would be a useful addition to the library.

Our project builds on Mathlib.LinearAlgebra.Matrix.Transvection, which already provides an algorithmic reduction of matrices to diagonal form using left and right transvections. Our formalization focuses specifically on reducing any matrix to lower triangular form using only left multiplication.

More precisely, we show that:

Given any matrix M, we can find a product of transvections and row exchange matrices L such that L * M is a lower triangular matrix.

Below is a brief overview of our approach:

  • rowEx i j: Explicit construction of row exchange matrices and proofs of their various properties.

  • EliminationStruct: A structure containing a list of transvections and a row exchange, used to inductively clear out columns.

Main Theorem:

Lean

theorem exists_list_elim_matrix_mul_eq_lowerTriangular (n : ℕ) (M : Matrix (Fin n) (Fin n) 𝕜) :
    ∃ LE : List (EliminationStruct (Fin n) 𝕜), (List.prod (List.map toElim LE) * M).BlockTriangular (OrderDual.toDual)

This proves that for any n×nn \times nn×n matrix M over a field, there exists a list of elimination structures LE such that multiplying their corresponding matrices on the left of M yields a lower triangular matrix.

You can view our full Lean file here: https://gist.github.com/Janav-Gupta/298eb701e488c6383a23686c606e7097

Please let us know if this would be a useful addition to the library, and if we should go ahead and open a PR. Thank you for your time, patience, and guidance!
Is it easy from your code to recover a constructive version? I.e. given some Matrix, give out a List (EliminationStruct (Fin n) 𝕜) such that the desired property holds.

I'm afraid I don't have time to look in detail at this work but you might consider seeing if you can connect with #38596 (which I expect to land in master very soon) and also docs#Echelon.Decomposition

Felix Pernegger said:

Is it easy from your code to recover a constructive version? I.e. given some Matrix, give out a List (EliminationStruct (Fin n) 𝕜) such that the desired property holds.

It is relatively easy, but not immediate. If there is interest, we can work on it.

Oliver Nash said:

I'm afraid I don't have time to look in detail at this work but you might consider seeing if you can connect with #38596 (which I expect to land in master very soon) and also docs#Echelon.Decomposition

As far as we could understand, #38596 is proving that the matrices of elementary row operations are members of GL(n,R)GL(n,\mathbb{R})GL(n,R). They also prove some group theoretic properties. We do not go into the group theory side at all.

As far as we could understand, docs#Echelon.Decomposition does not contain a proof of the Gaussian Elimination, but only contains:

  1. A verification of whether a give matrix is in Echelon form
  2. An expression of the rank of the matrix in terms of the number of pivots

We are new to Lean community and are not sure what kind of connection is expected. Could you please help us?
